feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with credible progression, clear public-sector specialization, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with more responsibility statements than outcome-driven achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing scope from coordinator to director; this strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Good specificity in platforms and scale: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, and 50+ publishers add substance.  
- Writing is polished and consistent overall, with a strong executive profile and relevant recent project examples.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: include impact on traffic, engagement, efficiency, adoption, campaign performance, or cost/time savings to increase impact.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these sections would improve structure and scannability.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; capitalization is slightly inconsistent (e.g., “organization-wide communications” vs. title-style section labels). No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and sector focus, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening the language and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Follow with a sharper second sentence: “Leads website transformation, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences that improve discovery, coordination, and performance across complex, mission-driven environments.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct verbs like “modernizing,” “leading,” or “scaling.”
- Use parallel phrasing and trim list length to keep the intro scannable.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- “Analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences” repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and use parallel phrasing: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial systems & publishing workflows • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search, automation & platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production, livestreaming & event operations
- Consider replacing “operations” repetition with more varied terms like “leadership,” “delivery,” or “optimization.”
- Keep this section at a higher level; let Technical + IT and Topline Skills carry the tools and platform specifics.
- Use “web” instead of “website” for a cleaner, more executive style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats the header and recent projects almost verbatim.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Multimedia production and livestream operations” are already covered in Topline Skills and work bullets.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats achievements already covered in recent roles and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will improve scanability.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects:” and format each item as a concise 1-line case example.
- Tighten wording: “AI-powered” may read more naturally than “AI-enabled,” and “10 x 20-foot” is more style-consistent than “10×20-foot.”
- Make each project more specific with one differentiator: audience, platform, scale, or purpose.
- Keep parallel structure: start each item with a strong verb and avoid stacking too many nouns in one sentence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with bullets in the current freelance and NACo roles.
- Consider keeping only 2–3 projects here or reframing them as “Selected projects” with details not already stated in Work Experience.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS

items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 4–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership language: “Built,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance for coordinated cross-channel communications.
- Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, campaign launches, time saved, search performance gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search and microsite work already appears in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and reserve specifics there.
- “Governance/analytics/workflows” repeats prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new or more advanced in this current engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational scope, and distinct senior-level achievements versus your earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific and measurable: add email performance, audience growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign impact if available.
- Tighten the remaining bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” / “Implemented analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery…” / “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo roles unless framed here as building new in-house production infrastructure.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: executional leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director role’s opening line.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior leadership scope rather than generic skill phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad nouns with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital communications strategy”; “Audience-focused content planning” → “Audience and journey-based content strategy.”
- Tighten and modernize the list to 4 bullets max, e.g.:
- Enterprise digital communications strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, advocacy and member-facing messaging
- Consider adding one higher-signal phrase tied to recent work: “AI-informed content discovery strategy” or “Platform and governance modernization.”
- Keep phrasing parallel and avoid mixing leadership, audience, and messaging concepts inconsistently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications leadership” substantially repeat Core Competencies and the header summary.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also echoes multiple recent NACo roles; keep it only if you remove a more repetitive line.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not every individual technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: “CMS modernization • API integrations • Workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Trim lower-signal items or move them to Technical + IT: remove “jQuery” and possibly “Airtable systems” from this topline section
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Technical + IT section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT,” so this section should emphasize strategic application and decision-making.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to outcome-oriented skills, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business language: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & performance optimization — GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and reporting • SEO and user behavior analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Avoid repeating every tool here if they are already listed elsewhere; use this section to signal senior-level analytical capability.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and older NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper, more senior phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with leadership-oriented wording: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio buildout and operations,” “PTZ camera direction.”
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera systems • Studio buildout and operations”
- Drop “virtual” if keeping “hybrid event delivery”; it’s implied and saves space.
- If this section allows nuance, prioritize capability over task wording: “In-house studio production” is stronger than “video editing” unless editing is central to target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrase.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in recent NACo experience, so this skills line should stay concise rather than restate duties.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use it to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than repeat a simple platform list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to a proficiency-based line, e.g.: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first and add brief qualifiers only where they reinforce recent impact.
- Standardize naming: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of “Power Pages.”
- If space allows, split by level: **Primary: Drupal | Working knowledge: WordPress, SharePoint, Microsoft Power Pages, GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one list or making this version more implementation-focused.
- Avoid repeating Drupal/WordPress in multiple sections unless one entry adds context such as enterprise migration or CMS architecture.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second phrase for delivery/integration: “Technical implementation: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, replace older/generic terms with stronger recent signals, e.g. “JavaScript” over “jQuery-first,” or add scope like “custom Drupal front-end implementation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) for cleaner phrasing unless ATS targeting requires them

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; either shorten this item or make Topline Skills more strategic and this section more tool-specific
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid adding it here unless tied to GitHub Actions or Cloudflare Workers specifically

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Workflow Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth: “Built and managed workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; coordinated delivery in Jira, Asana and Trello.”
- Cut one lower-value/redundant platform if space is tight (likely Basecamp or Trello) and prioritize tools tied to recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support a workflow/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tools to include, but this item is currently just a vendor list and undersells your recent leadership of email operations. It should signal platform depth and align with the NACo roles without repeating newsletter achievements already covered in experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Newsletter publishing workflows • Audience segmentation**
- If accurate, add one higher-value capability instead of more tools: **template management**, **list hygiene**, **journey automation**, or **performance optimization**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was minimal/older exposure, remove it to keep the list credible and current

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding metrics here like “tens of thousands reached”; that impact is already covered well in Work Experience
- Don’t repeat broad phrases like “multi-channel communications,” which already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In a recent, senior CV, this section should read as a concise tools list or add clearer optimization depth.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and modernize the phrasing: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Replace **Dashboarding** with the actual platforms already listed; “dashboarding” is an activity, not a tool.
- If accurate, swap in more specific terms with stronger signal: **KPI reporting**, **conversion analysis**, **behavior analytics**, or **experiment design**.
- Keep this section tool-led; save impact statements like analytics expansion or reporting improvements for recent NACo/freelance experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider deleting one or making this version strictly tools-only.
- **SEO** also overlaps with broader strategy language elsewhere; **SEO analysis** is more precise.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with concrete outputs rather than team/channel leadership language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function and improve production workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Add specific deliverables: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams, weekly video updates and other multimedia content for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing so it doesn’t compete with later leadership roles: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing tasks.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; distinguish this as production/execution, not channel ownership.
- Avoid repeating broad “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” language already used in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; produced digital and multimedia content to extend member-facing communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and strongest proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to” with stronger verbs such as “produced,” “supported,” or “led,” depending on accuracy.
- If available, add one concrete outcome: number of episodes launched, audience growth, internal adoption, or how content supported advocacy/member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broad “digital content production” language that repeats later web/video leadership roles.
- Don’t overstate multimedia leadership here if those responsibilities expanded more substantially in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item reads a bit mixed—software, workflows, and production capabilities are bundled together. Tightening it will make it feel more senior and reduce overlap with the stronger multimedia leadership points in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Separate tools from capabilities; keep this item software-focused and concise.
- Use broader, professional phrasing: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- Replace generic “Livestream studio workflows” with a clearer capability if you keep it here: “Livestream production” or “Studio production workflows”
- Consider adding level/context only if true and useful: “Podcast production (planning, recording, editing)” or “Broadcast-quality video editing”
